clue.text: It sticks tongue against part of mouth

parts.note: the gums are the flesh around the teeth, a part of the mouth
a tongue is a language, here the language of the Arab world

explanation.surface: A dentist's oddity: something that clings to the tongue against the inside of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' simply sets the two pieces side by side. 'It sticks' is the definition, treating the clue's 'It' as the thing being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: This acacia resin has long been used as a water-soluble glue, for example on stamps and envelopes.

clue.text: Spicy drink inadequate for group of friends

indicators.note: something inadequate falls short, so the drink's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a posset is an old hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale and spiced

explanation.surface: A mulled drink served in too small a measure for a gathering of mates.
explanation.walkthrough: A POSSET, an old British bedtime drink, is cut short by 'inadequate', losing its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a posse is a gang or crowd of companions, extended from the sheriff's band of men.

clue.text: Careful: there's a split in your case

indicators.note: the split sits in the casing formed by the word for your, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: A warning to be cautious because the casing of something you own has cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in your case' means inside the word for 'your', which acts as the casing; 'case' tempts a reading as 'in your situation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrifty is careful with money, spending sparingly and avoiding waste.

clue.text: Sweet girls with hidden power that are knockouts

indicators.note: the girls carry the power concealed inside them, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: cuties are sweet, attractive girls
P is the standard symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Pretty young women with secret strength who are stunning beauties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockouts' looks like slang for stunning girls, continuing the surface; it actually means elimination matches. P goes inside CUTIES.
explanation.definitionFit: In British football cup competitions every tie is a knockout match: the loser is eliminated.

clue.text: Spin doctor one has to follow

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first, so it is placed after it

parts.note: one has is I've, the contraction of I have, with I as one

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor's sidekick says he must trail behind his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' looks like a single phrase; split it so 'Spin' is the definition. 'one has' reads as I'VE (I have).
explanation.definitionFit: A spin in a car is a short pleasure trip, the same as going for a drive.

clue.text: Glower, a long time left in the dark

indicators.note: the long time and left are placed inside the dark, one piece inside another

parts.note: night is the dark, as in 'after dark'
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Someone scowled after being left alone for ages without light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl, but read it as 'one that glows'; 'in' puts the long time and left inside the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing gas tube used in signs is something that glows, read whimsically as a 'glow-er'.

clue.text: Break, whether or not resistance is maintained

definitions.text: Break, whether or not resistance is maintained

parts.words: Break, whether or not resistance is maintained
parts.note: the word for break stays a word for break whether or not R, the symbol for resistance, is kept inside it: with R or as BUST, both mean break

explanation.surface: A rupture that happens regardless of whether opposition holds out.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break open suddenly, as a balloon or pipe does under pressure.

clue.text: Risky driver's back, one that's maybe crashed, right?

parts.note: the tail is the back end of something
a gate may be crashed by someone getting into a party uninvited, a gatecrasher

explanation.surface: A dangerous motorist is back after a crash, asking if that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' suggests a car accident; it is gatecrashing, entering a party uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who follows too closely behind another vehicle drives dangerously, and is called by this name.

clue.text: Man at short cover is rebellious

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word for cover is abbreviated, losing its tail

parts.note: insurance is cover against loss
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at short cover is unruly; short cover being a fielding position near the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Short cover is a cricket fielding position, which disguises the parse: 'short' trims the word for cover to its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent person rises in revolt against authority, so is rebellious; the word works as an adjective too.

clue.text: Root of folk dance not initially apparent

indicators.note: the word's first letter cannot be seen, so the opening letter of the dance is dropped

parts.note: the morris is a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks

explanation.surface: The origins of a country dance tradition are obscure at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: MORRIS dancing is a traditional English folk dance; 'not initially apparent' takes away its M. 'Root of' reads as origin, but 'Root' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root is the fragrant dried rootstock of certain irises, used in perfume.

clue.text: Uninvolved supporter released after City has dropped appeal

indicators.note: the word for released comes after the trimmed city

parts.note: a fan is a supporter, as of a football club

indicators.note: the city loses something, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal
free means released

explanation.surface: A football fan is let go after his City side lose their attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has dropped' takes IT (sex appeal) out of CITY, leaving CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fancy-free is not romantically attached or committed to anyone, hence uninvolved.

clue.text: Browser that's no good dropped by country

indicators.note: the country lets these letters go, so they are removed from it

parts.note: England is a country

explanation.surface: An internet browser that is useless gets abandoned by a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' suggests web software; here it is an animal that browses, feeding on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope that feeds by browsing on shrubs and trees.

clue.text: In a wine store, head of Salvation Army not to be tempted?

indicators.note: the head of Salvation and the Army go into the wine store, one piece inside another

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store for wine bottles

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve army

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army officer in a wine cellar resists temptation, as the teetotal Salvation Army would.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; the Salvation Army is famously teetotal, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from indulging, especially from alcohol, so to resist being tempted.

clue.text: Visits restaurant, getting seat thus?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: its first word with the second as an anagram signal rearranges to the clue word seat

explanation.surface: Someone dining out wonders whether that's how to get a table.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, rearranges EATS 'out' of order to give SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home.

clue.text: Chapter in story turned into great success

indicators.note: the chapter goes inside the story, one piece placed within another
turned means turned round, so the story is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: One chapter in a novel became a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TALE to ELAT, and C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, borrowed from the French word for splendour.

clue.text: Places to broadcast mass medium production

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Locations where a mass will be transmitted on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' is a spiritualist, not a broadcasting medium, and 'mass' is M, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance supposedly exuded by a spiritualist during a seance.

clue.text: Coming up, remove restriction from offender kept in

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: to de-tag an offender is to remove the electronic tag restricting their movements

explanation.surface: An offender is released from a curfew tag while still detained.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is British school and court slang for confined to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or offender who is gated is confined to a place as a punishment, so kept in.

clue.text: In festival month, hanging round archaeology site

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the hanging goes around the site

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry wall hanging
a dig is an archaeological excavation site

explanation.surface: During a carnival month, tapestries hang around an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'round' has the tapestry wrap the excavation, with the month's single-letter abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the carnival celebrated on Shrove Tuesday, famously in New Orleans and Rio.

clue.text: Not unknown for canteen to stock litres, one thinks

indicators.note: the canteen holds the litres in stock, so that piece goes inside
Not tells us to leave out the unknown from the canteen's word

parts.note: a refectory is a dining hall or canteen in a college or monastery
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A known quantity rather than unknown for a canteen keeping litres in stock, one supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, an algebra unknown, leaves REFECTORY to give REFECTOR, then L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflector is a person who reflects, that is who thinks deeply or ponders.

clue.text: Sketches show, in the past, the other side of the border

definitions.meaning: a celebrated 1960s British satirical comedy revue of sketches

definitions.text: the other side of the border
definitions.meaning: beyond the outer edge, the fringe being the border

explanation.walkthrough: The revue began at the Edinburgh Festival in 1960, starring Peter Cook, Dudley Moore, Alan Bennett and Jonathan Miller.
explanation.definitionFit: The revue's title also literally means past the edge, as a fringe is a border.

clue.text: Interloper making the tennis?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: its first word, meaning crazy, is an anagram signal acting on the rest, which rearranges to the clue words the tennis

explanation.surface: An intruder disrupting the tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'cuckoo' (mad) scrambles the following words to give 'the tennis'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds' nests, so the phrase names an unwelcome intruder.

clue.text: Pressure on a colleague from the highest authority

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: An order to lean on a co-worker that comes straight from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets P before A and PAL in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something papal comes from the Pope, the highest authority in the Roman Catholic church.

clue.text: Police operation gets thieves' leader in to confess

indicators.note: the leader of the thieves gets in, placed inside the word for confess

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A police undercover job persuades the gang boss to come in and own up.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of thieves goes inside SING, criminal slang for confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is an undercover operation in which police trap criminals with a deception.

clue.text: How to spread the cost of undemanding schooling

definitions.meaning: buying by instalments on generous credit arrangements
school periods that are not hard, read as easy school terms

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes terms as the periods of a school year.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are payment by instalments; read literally, easy school terms are undemanding schooling.

clue.text: Cheese faces melting in a bag

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: melting means losing shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Cheese runs as it melts inside a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese faces' tempts an anagram of both words; only 'faces' melts, after BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat case or bag for carrying papers.

clue.text: Progress that is inflexible as iron, with favourites upset

parts.note: a goose is a tailor's smoothing iron with a long curved handle

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Rigid progress hard as iron, with the favoured ones overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as iron' looks like a simile for inflexible; it is the tailor's iron called a GOOSE. PETS turned up reads STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose step is a stiff-legged military march, a way of advancing without bending the knee.

clue.text: Sailor grinding organ at a port

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: grinding means crushing up, so the organ's letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor plays a barrel organ at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grinding' suggests a barrel organ being cranked; it is the anagram signal, rearranging the organ's letters to RAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Catalonia, Spain.

clue.text: Spacemen needing line of passage?

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency, staffed by astronauts

explanation.surface: Astronauts in need of a route through space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' means the nasal passage; the question mark flags that a nose is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, as in the nasal passages.

clue.text: Still covers like fungus

indicators.note: the word for still wraps around the word for like

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
as means like

explanation.surface: Something still lies under a fungal coating.
explanation.walkthrough: YET covers AS: YE-AS-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a single-celled fungus used in brewing and baking.

clue.text: Fact prosecutor put before corporation

indicators.note: the prosecutor comes first, placed before the second piece

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A prosecutor sets a key fact before a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is old British slang for a large belly, hence TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or piece of information.
